text.en: Met Éireann's eastern radar stands at Dublin Airport and has watched the east of Ireland and the Irish Sea since 1991. It was upgraded in 2010 but is still a single-polarisation radar; its replacement and relocation are being planned as part of a programme to grow Ireland's network from two radars to six.

Ireland's western radar stands at Shannon Airport on the Shannon estuary, where a radar has worked since 1996. In October 2023 it was replaced by Ireland's first dual-polarisation radar, which covers a 240 km radius over the west of the country and the Atlantic approaches.
